title: Next-gen memory pipeline features — fresh 2026 research on Mem0, Microsoft Agent Framework, and Oracle AI Agent Memory
description: Distinct from EPIC-2 (Cosmos-inspired, Done) and EPIC-3 (Oracle-inspired, Done) — those two epics were scoped from the July 2026 snapshot in ai-agent-platform-competitive-analysis.md. This epic is grounded in dedicated follow-up research (2026-07-31) into the exact pipeline mechanics of three platforms that survey only summarized at a high level: Mem0's real-time per-write ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP classification (candidate fact compared via cosine similarity to top-k existing memories, an LLM policy routes the outcome) as distinct from this SDK's existing ENH-3 Reconciler (which only batch-scans already-written facts for contradictions); Microsoft Agent Framework's `ContextProvider`/`HistoryProvider` lifecycle-hook adapter shape (`before_run`/`after_run`, GA as of April 2026 — confirmed via current Microsoft Learn docs, dated 2026-07-10), a fundamentally different integration pattern than the Step 6 LangChain/OpenAI-Agents/MCP adapters; and Oracle AI Agent Memory's 26.6 release (hybrid semantic+keyword search now GA, context-card per-type minimum-result balancing, `MemoryExtractionConfig`) which shipped after EPIC-3 was originally scoped. Also picks up two items VER-13's market-fit check left as documented PARTIAL/open: hybrid retrieval and ergonomic GDPR-style erasure. Same Step 0 philosophy as every prior epic: Db2-only, zero mandatory new infrastructure, developer-controlled writes by default — every new hook here (`IngestResolver`, hybrid search, the new adapter) is opt-in and leaves today's default behavior unchanged. See the dated DECISIONS.md entry for the full research writeup, including what was deliberately not turned into a story and why.
